message: Review complete: 3 finding(s) across 1 selected item(s).

comments.content: The rolling `tail` buffer never discards already-processed lines: every `pull` re-feeds the entire window (minus bytes that fell off the 4KB cap) to `trackSseLine`. The consecutive-duplicate collapse only dedupes adjacent repeats, so on any multi-chunk stream (i.e. every real SSE stream) re-processed old lines interleave with new ones. Failure scenario: the 4KB window holds `event: content_block_start` and `event: content_block_delta` and the next chunk adds no new event → processing re-pushes `content_block_start` (last entry is `delta`), then re-pushes `content_block_delta`, so `trace.eventTypes` grows by ~2 entries per chunk and the log's `slice(-6)`/`slice(-12)` windows print e.g. `start > delta > start > delta > start > delta` instead of the true final ordering. On the long tool-heavy streams under investigation this masks the exact event-sequence evidence the wrapper exists to collect. Fix: process only complete new lines each pull and retain just the trailing partial line (flushing it on done), e.g. split after decode, `tail = lines.pop() ?? ""` (capped), and iterate the popped-complete lines. Note: keep the done-branch flush of the residual `tail` so a final unterminated `[DONE]` line is still detected.

Cancel/read race: if the consumer cancels while a `pull` is awaiting `reader.read()`, `reader.cancel(reason)` in the cancel handler resolves that pending read as `{done: true}` (per the streams spec), so this done branch then runs after the "stream cancelled by consumer" log: it (a) emits a fabricated "stream ended without a terminal event" line whenever no terminal was seen yet — an abort-induced false positive of the exact signature issue #9 is hunting, polluting the evidence channel — and (b) calls `controller.close()` on a stream that cancel already closed, which throws a TypeError inside `pull` (swallowed by the stream machinery). Failure scenario: harness aborts/cleans up a long streaming call between chunks → pm2 log contains both the cancel line and a bogus no-terminal line for the same request. Fix: set a `cancelled` flag in the cancel handler and skip both the log and `controller.close()` in the done branch when it is set.

Reconstructed Response throws on null-body statuses: `!response.ok` is true for 101/204/205/304, and per the fetch spec the Response constructor throws `TypeError: Response with null body status cannot have body` whenever the status is a null-body status and body is non-null — `body` here is always a non-null string (`""` counts as non-null; only `null` is allowed). Failure scenario: gateway/intermediary (proxy, LB) answers POST /messages with 204/205/304 → `new Response(body, { status: 204, ... })` throws → the outer catch logs it misleadingly as "zhipu-fetch: transport failed" and rethrows → @ai-sdk/anthropic receives a fetch-level rejection (no status code, no error body) instead of the actual HTTP response that native fetch would have returned. This both breaks the byte-for-byte pass-through promise and destroys the very evidence (an unusual gateway status) this wrapper exists to capture. Pass `null` as the body for null-body statuses.
comments.thinking:
Confirmed the two `new Response` construction sites. The non-2xx branch at line 147 is the one with the null-body status hazard.

Analysis summary of the whole diff:

1. **Null-body status TypeError (new finding)**: `!response.ok` includes 101/204/205/304. `new Response(body, { status: 204 })` throws `TypeError` per the fetch spec ("If init['status'] is a null-body status and body is non-null, then throw a TypeError") — and `body` is always a non-null string here (`""` is still non-null). The throw is caught by the outer catch, mislogged as "transport failed", and rethrown — so the SDK receives a transport rejection with no HTTP status/body instead of the actual response. Native fetch returns these responses normally. This is a deterministic contract break on a legal HTTP input, in the exact branch the author flagged for review. Fix: pass `null` as the body for null-body statuses.

2. Everything else checked out:
   - Backpressure: pull-based with default HWM 1 preserves one-chunk-at-a-time demand; byte-for-byte same chunk objects enqueued.
   - Reader lifecycle: on underlying error the reader auto-releases (stream errored); on done it auto-releases; cancel propagates via `reader.cancel(reason)` — no leak.
   - Header deletion (content-encoding/content-length) is required and correct for both reconstructed Response paths.
   - SSE heuristic false-positives/negatives and log-symmetry issues are excluded by the user's stated boundaries; tail reprocessing and the cancel/read race are already reported.

Report the single new finding, then task_done.
